Marathon Petroleum edged up 0.31% today to close at $388.90, continuing a strong two-week rally that has seen the stock climb 7.81%. The gains reflect escalating Middle East tensions—specifically renewed military exchanges between the U.S. and Iran over the past few days that have pushed crude oil prices to six-week highs and sent gasoline to record levels for Labor Day. For a refiner like Marathon, higher crude and product prices typically expand refining margins, and U.S. refineries are running at 98% capacity, leaving little room to boost output but plenty of room to benefit from elevated pricing.

The broader tailwind is straightforward: geopolitical risk premiums are building into oil prices as the conflict heats up, and refiners are positioned to profit when crude rises faster than they can pass costs through to customers. With oil inventories moderate and gasoline prices already at historic highs, the market is pricing in sustained demand and margin strength for companies that turn crude into fuel.
